title: Cost of electricity (kWh)
examples: How do I know if I am using too much electricity?
What does kWh stand for on my bill?
Is using LED bulbs really cheaper in the long run?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the cost of using electricity.
The unit for electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour, or kWh.
One kilowatt-hour means using one thousand watts for one full hour.
Your electricity bill shows how many kWh you have used over a period.
The cost is calculated by multiplying the total kWh by the price per kWh.

draw.text: Cost = kWh used x Price per kWh

explain.say: In real life, a large appliance like a heater uses a lot of energy quickly.

faq.q: What is the difference between watts and kilowatt-hours?
faq.a: Watts measure power right now, while kilowatt-hours measure total energy used over time. You can think of watts as speed, and kWh as distance traveled.
asks: What is the difference between power and energy?
Is wattage the same as energy?
How do I calculate total energy?

faq.q: Do I need to check my bill every month?
faq.a: It is helpful to check your bill to monitor your energy use. This helps you spot patterns of high usage that you can then try to reduce.
asks: Should I look at my energy bill often?
How can I track my energy use?
What does a spike on my bill mean?

faq.q: If I use less electricity, will my bill automatically go down?
faq.a: Yes, generally speaking, less kWh used means a lower total cost. However, some bills have fixed daily charges too.
asks: Does using less power mean less money?
Are there fixed charges on electricity bills?
What affects the total cost besides kWh?

faq.q: What does the 'kW' part of kWh mean?
faq.a: The 'kW' stands for kilowatt, which is a unit of power. It is one thousand watts, a measure of how fast energy is used.
asks: Is kilowatt the same as a lot of power?
How is kilowatt related to watts?

faq.q: Are there times when electricity is cheaper to use?
faq.a: Some energy suppliers offer different rates depending on the time of day. You should check your specific tariff details for this information.
asks: Do different times cost different amounts?

facts: One kilowatt-hour is the amount of energy used by a 1000-watt bulb for one hour.
The unit kWh measures total energy consumed, not just the rate of use.
Electricity bills show the total kWh used over the billing period.
Reducing energy use directly lowers the kWh amount and the cost.

quiz.say: A device uses 500 watts of power for two hours. How many kWh did it use?
quiz.why: You must convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by one thousand, making it zero point five kilowatts. Then multiply by two hours to get one kWh.

wrong.0: You might incorrectly add the power and time together instead of multiplying.
wrong.2: You might multiply all the numbers together, but you must convert the unit first.
wrong.3: You might forget to convert watts to kilowatts, which is a necessary step.

quiz.say: If the rate is 0 point 20 per kWh and you use 300 kWh, what is the cost?
quiz.why: You multiply the total energy used, three hundred kWh, by the cost rate of zero point two zero to find the total charge.

wrong.0: You might forget to multiply by the rate and just use the kWh number.
wrong.2: You might add the numbers together instead of multiplying them.
wrong.3: You might divide the two numbers because you see them next to each other.

quiz.say: If a toaster uses 1000 watts and runs for one hour, what is the energy used?
quiz.why: Since one thousand watts is exactly one kilowatt, using it for one hour gives you exactly one kilowatt-hour.

wrong.0: You might leave the unit as watt-hours instead of converting it to the required kWh.
wrong.1: You might think that because it is only one hour, no energy was used at all.
wrong.3: You might forget to divide the watts by one thousand to get kilowatts.
